header: THE SAME NEWS BY MEANING. Rules about names and figures (steel.ts clusterTopics, priority.ts assignDesk) join the headlines that name the same companies or carry the same figures, but they cannot know that two headlines that share no name and no figure say the same thing in two languages. For that I use the embedding model the intranet already uses for its circular search (Gemini gemini-embedding-001, GEMINI_API_KEY): it turns a headline into a vector in a space where the same meaning is near, whatever the language, so two headlines are the same news when their vectors are close (cosine similarity). WHAT GOES TO GOOGLE: only the headlines of public news feeds, nothing that anybody typed. WHAT IT COSTS: a headline is about 30 tokens; a batch of 100 is one call; a headline already embedded is kept in memory (and never asked again while this server process lives), so after the first minute only the headlines that are new are sent: a few calls an hour. WHEN IT FAILS (no key, no answer, over quota) it returns nothing and the rules alone decide; it never throws. This is a second opinion ADDED to the rules, never a replacement: the rules are free, instant and explain themselves; the vectors only catch what the rules cannot.

doc: Embeds the headlines (the ones not yet kept) in batches and returns a map of every headline that has a vector. A batch that fails is left out; nothing is thrown. `fetchImpl` is for the tests.

symbols.name: SHORTLIST
doc: The similarity at or above which two headlines are put to the judge. Headlines of one trade are all near each other (the steel headlines of a day are 0.88 to 0.95 apart, the real duplicates among the top of them), so a number alone cannot say "same news": it only picks the pairs worth asking about.

symbols.name: MAX_PAIRS
doc: The most pairs put to the judge in one asking (the nearest first).

symbols.name: pairKey
symbols.sig: const pairKey = (a: string, b: string): string =>
doc: One pair, as a key that is the same whichever headline comes first.

symbols.name: judgePrompt
symbols.sig: export function judgePrompt(pairs: Array<[string, string]>): string
doc: What the judge is told. It decides the SAME NEWS: the same thing happened or was announced, told by two papers or in two languages; the same company or topic is not enough, and different figures are different news.

symbols.name: parseJudge
symbols.sig: export function parseJudge(text: string, count: number): number[]
doc: Reads the judge's JSON: the numbers of the pairs it called the same (anything unreadable is "none").

symbols.name: JUDGE_MODELS
doc: The models of the judge: the lite one first (1.2 s for eight pairs, where the ordinary flash model took 3 s and, with twenty pairs, more than 12 s: it thinks at length), then the chat chain; never a Pro one (src/lib/ai/noPro.ts).

symbols.name: PAIRS_PER_ASKING
doc: The pairs of one asking of the judge: more are split into several askings that go together.

symbols.name: geminiJudge
doc: The judge: the intranet's own light Gemini model, JSON out, temperature 0. Returns null when it cannot answer.

symbols.name: meaningLinks
symbols.sig: export async function meaningLinks(titles: string[], opts: { embed?: typeof embedHeadlines; judge?: Judge } = {}): Promise<Set<string>>
doc: THE PAIRS OF HEADLINES THAT ARE THE SAME NEWS BY MEANING, as a set of pairKeys. Step 1: the vectors of the headlines (embedHeadlines) pick the nearest pairs (SHORTLIST, at most MAX_PAIRS). Step 2: the judge decides which of them are the same news; its answer is kept for each pair, so a pair is asked once. If the vectors or the judge are not there, the set is empty and the rules alone decide.

symbols.name: meaningOf
symbols.sig: const meaningOf = (a: string, b: string): boolean =>
doc: Has the judge said these two headlines are the same news? Instant (it only looks at what the judge has already said); false when the pair was never asked. This is what the builders of the lists take.

symbols.name: forgetHeadlines
doc: For the tests: forget what is kept.

symbols.name: dropSameMeaning
symbols.sig: export function dropSameMeaning<T extends { title: string; source: string; also?: string[] }>(items: T[], same: (a: string, b: string) => boolean = meaningOf): T[]
symbols.generics: T extends { title: string; source: string; also?: string[] }
doc: ONE ROW FOR ONE NEWS, BEFORE THE ANSWER GOES: of two stories of a list that the judge has called the same news (meaningOf), the first stays and names the other paper. The route asks the judge about the list's own headlines first (meaningLinks, within a time limit), so that the repeat is never shown, not even the first time; a pair the judge has not answered stays as it is.

behaviours: the judge's answer is read from JSON, even inside other words; anything unreadable, or a number out of range, is 'none'
the prompt numbers the pairs, says what 'same news' means (not merely the same company; different figures are different), and asks for JSON only
230 headlines go in 3 calls of at most 100, each comes back as a vector of length one
a headline already embedded is never sent again: the next asking sends only the one new headline
with no key, or when the service refuses or is unreachable, it returns nothing and never throws
only pairs at ${SHORTLIST} or nearer are put to the judge (the three ALPHA headlines, not BETA or GAMMA), and only the pair it calls the same comes back
the verdict is kept: asked again, the judge is not called, and meaningOf answers at once, in either order; a pair never asked is not the same
when the judge cannot answer (null), nothing is joined: the rules alone decide
never more than ${MAX_PAIRS} pairs in all, however many headlines are close, split into askings of at most ${PAIRS_PER_ASKING}
one asking that fails leaves its pairs unasked (not 'different', and asked again next time); the other asking still counts: 28 pairs in two askings of 15 and 13, the first failing, 13 joined
no key: the judge says nothing and the call costs nothing
the steel list: two headlines that share no name and no figure stay two rows by the rules, and become one when the judge has said they are the same news

the priority desk: the same death in English and Hindi with no name in either is told apart by the rules, and joined (one story, in the language that arrived first) when the judge says so; a death and an accident are never joined
the route answers at once with what the judge has already said, and puts the new headlines to it AFTER the answer has gone (next/server after), never making a reader wait for the model
only the headlines of public feeds are sent, nothing typed; the model is the chat chain (never a Pro one) and the embedding model the circular search uses
with more near pairs than the cap (all 136 pairs are at cosine 1), the pair that shares three words or more is put to the judge first and is not lost
dropSameMeaning joins the two stories the judge called the same news (the first stays and names the other paper) and leaves the rest
with no verdict (the judge never asked, or down) the list stays as it is
the route asks the judge about the list's own headlines BEFORE the answer goes (not only afterwards), for at most 4 s, then joins
